summary: Comparison between two periods: current and previous values with proportional bars and a percentage change badge, with the direction written out for screen readers.
whenToUse: Compare a metric between the current and previous period (month, quarter, year).
Highlight whether a change is positive or negative relative to the business goal.
whenNotToUse: Trends over many periods: use LineChart or KpiCard with a trend line.
Comparisons between more than two values: use BarChart or RankingCard.

props.name: formatOptions
props.description: Value format (and of the absolute difference when the previous value is 0).

props.name: higherIsBetter
props.description: Whether an increase is positive; with false, a decrease is shown as positive (e.g. errors, durations).

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: When set, the label becomes a heading of that level.

inherits: HTML attributes of <div> (id, style, data-*, aria-*).
accessibility: Periods and values are a description list (<dl>): period name in <dt>, formatted value in <dd>.
The direction of the change is written out for screen readers (“increase”, “decrease”, “unchanged”), not conveyed only by arrow or color.
Bars are aria-hidden: values are always text.
In forced-colors mode the badge has a border and the bars use Highlight/GrayText.
responsive: Rows span the full width; the badge wraps below the label in narrow containers.
Use Grid with minItemWidth to place multiple comparisons side by side.
customization: Tokens: --dc-look-radius-container, --dc-gradient-accent / --dc-color-data-1 for the current bar, --dc-color-border-strong for the previous one, feedback surfaces and foregrounds for the badge.
commonMistakes: Forgetting higherIsBetter={false} for metrics where a decrease is positive.
Passing already formatted values as strings: numbers are required to compute bars and change.
Comparing periods of different length without stating it in the period label.

examples.name: Dashboard
examples.title: Multiple comparisons
examples.description: Responsive grid, including a previous period equal to 0.

limits: When the previous value is 0 the percentage is undefined: the badge shows the formatted absolute difference.
Bars are proportional to absolute values: with negative values they only indicate magnitude.
